title: 14 NEW MSFS Marketplace Activities: Lufthansa Missions, A220 Challenges & Global Hubs!
description:
Ready to take control of commercial airliner operations across the globe in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020? The Marketplace just received 14 brand new featured releases—headlined by Lufthansa's European schedule, precision A220 landing challenges across every continent, discounted airline collection bundles, and an extensive worldwide rollout of real-world airline fleet and airport hub schedules from VA Systems!

In this structured marketplace breakdown, we cut through the storefront clutter and organize these arrivals into logical categories with key aircraft compatibility notes to help you plan your next departure:

✈️ COMMERCIAL AIRLINE MISSIONS & CHALLENGES (LUFTHANSA, A220 & MASTER BUNDLES)
Step into scheduled line operations with structured commercial activity packs from Perfect Flight. We examine "12 Legs Lufthansa Fall 2026," featuring 12 real-world European IFR rotations for the default Asobo A320neo V1 with in-game briefings, custom audio, and over 100 monitored flight events. Looking for savings? The "Summer 2026 Master Collection #2" bundles previous Air New Zealand, Iberia, and ITA Airways rotations for the iniBuilds A320neo V2 at a steep discount. Plus, test your stick-and-rudder skills with "Advanced Challenges: A220 Landings," delivering 24 demanding global approaches across 7 continents for the Virtualcol A220 series!

🌐 GLOBAL AIRLINE FLEET SCHEDULES (VA SYSTEMS)
Eliminate the guesswork of where to fly next with authentic airline fleet schedules and real-world liveries. This week's drop introduces dedicated schedule packages for Aerolíneas Argentinas, Eurowings, Vietnam Airlines, Scandinavian Airlines (SAS), and Viva Aerobus (requires ownership of the matching base aircraft).

🛫 INTERNATIONAL HUB TRAFFIC OVERHAULS (VA SYSTEMS)
Transform major commercial gateways into bustling international operational centers. New multi-airline hub traffic packs arrive for Fukuoka (RJFF), Stockholm Arlanda (ESSA), Boston Logan (KBOS), Manila Ninoy Aquino (RPLL), and Carrasco International (SUMU)—equipping regional ramps and international terminals with authentic carrier departures and liveries.

Whether you're testing your flare technique in the A220, flying scheduled European vectors with Lufthansa, or populating busy international hubs with authentic traffic, these additions bring structured operational depth to your simulator.

Which of these packages are you loading into your flight computer first? Let us know in the comments below!

If you find these marketplace breakdowns helpful, don't forget to hit the like button, subscribe for weekly flight sim coverage, and clear skies on your next flight!
